findings.title: RESIDUAL No backup, restore, RPO/RTO or point-in-time-recovery procedure exists anywhere
evidence: [E:cmd#27 git ls-files | grep -iE backup|restore|pg_dump -> only app/src/main/res/xml/backup_rules.xml (Android auto-backup rules)]
[E:cmd#27 git grep -i backup|pg_dump|restore over yml/yaml/sh/js -> no server match]
[E:LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md T-1 day requires backups completed and an isolated restore test meeting documented RPO/RTO]
findings.impact: backup/restore scripts written and their tool preflight and populated-DB refusal executed (exit 4 with a clear message). No real pg_dump/pg_restore round-trip: postgresql-client is absent from this sandbox. RPO/RTO documented but the drill is not done. || original impact: The database holds phone numbers, KYC document references, payment intents and an append-only ledger. A lost volume is unrecoverable and the ledger cannot be reconstructed.
findings.remediation: Script pg_dump/pg_restore on a schedule, record RPO/RTO, add a restore-drill step to the runbook. Managed Postgres with PITR is the cheaper path for a Render pilot.

findings.title: RESIDUAL: a zero-width-named workflow still builds the APK with lint and tests disabled
evidence: [E:cmd git ls-files .github/workflows -> 'android-apk.yml', 'build.yml', '\u200capkbuild.yml' (the third filename begins with U+200C ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER)]
[E:.github/workflows/‌apkbuild.yml:L26 run: ./gradlew assembleDebug -x lint -x test --no-daemon]
[E:.github/workflows/android-apk.yml:L47 ./gradlew test --stacktrace and :L69 assembleDebug WITHOUT -x test - the correct workflow already exists]
[E:cmd git cat-file -e HEAD:ci/android-apk.yml and HEAD:github/workflows/build.yml both fail - the two stale duplicates were deleted in 3983342]
findings.impact: Three workflows build the same APK. Two of them (android-apk.yml, build.yml) run the tests; the third skips lint and tests outright with -x lint -x test, so it goes green on an APK whose tests fail. Because its filename starts with a zero-width non-joiner it is near-impossible to select, edit or delete by typing its name, which is why it survived. Deleting the two duplicate orphan files - the other half of this finding - was completed in 3983342.
findings.exploit_or_repro: Executed diffs and filename byte inspection.
findings.remediation: Delete .github/workflows/‌apkbuild.yml and keep android-apk.yml, which already runs ./gradlew test before assembleDebug. Requires the `workflows` permission, so this stays requires_human. The duplicate ci/ and github/ orphans named in the original finding are already gone.

findings.title: RESIDUAL Dockerfile base image is a floating tag, not pinned by digest
evidence: [E:services/auth-api/Dockerfile:L7 FROM node:22-alpine - floating tag, no @sha256: digest]
[E:services/auth-api/Dockerfile:L1-L6 the reason is recorded in-file rather than silently skipped]
[E:services/auth-api/Dockerfile:L9 ENV NODE_ENV=production - PRESENT]
[E:services/auth-api/Dockerfile:L23-L24 HEALTHCHECK against /health - PRESENT]
[E:services/auth-api/Dockerfile:L26 USER node - non-root]
[E:cmd#1 hub.docker.com and registry-1.docker.io both SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL from this sandbox]
findings.impact: A rebuilt image can silently pull a different node:22-alpine than the one that was tested. The other two thirds of the original finding (no HEALTHCHECK, no NODE_ENV) are closed and are no longer claimed as open.
findings.remediation: Run `docker buildx imagetools inspect node:22-alpine` on a host with registry access and replace the tag with the resolved `node:22-alpine@sha256:<digest>`.

findings.title: server.js is a 1297-line god file holding all 27 routes, validation and money logic
evidence: [E:cmd wc -l services/auth-api/src/*.js -> server.js 1297, migrate.js 114, retry.js 90; 27 registered routes]
findings.impact: Every change to auth, AI, KYC, orders, devices, payments and escrow touches one file, raising merge-conflict and regression risk exactly where the money lives. The file has grown from 694 to 1297 lines and 16 to 27 routes during this remediation, so the concentration has roughly doubled rather than been reduced.
findings.remediation: Extract route groups into modules sharing one app factory; keep the ledger and state machine in domain modules.

findings.title: RESIDUAL: real Zarinpal round-trip unexecuted - the capture logic itself is now integration-tested offline
evidence: [E:cmd harness J5.1 -> POST /v1/payments/zarinpal/start returned 502 payment_unavailable; sandbox.zarinpal.com is unreachable from the audit sandbox]

[E:test test/capture.test.js with test/zarinpal-stub.mjs preloaded via node --import -> callback with a validly signed state captured escrow_liability 120000 / technician_payable 680000 / gateway_clearing 800000, ledger net 0]
[E:test same lane -> one escrow_holds row for 120000 not due immediately; intent, quote and order all advanced to paid; provider_ref_id stored]
[E:test same lane -> replayed redirect produced no second payment_capture entry and no second hold (idempotent)]
[E:test same lane -> forged state rejected 400; ZARINPAL_STUB_VERIFY_CODE=-1 returned 502 with zero ledger entries and zero holds]
[E:test negative control: changing the split to 0.20 made the assertion fail with escrow_liability 160000, so the test can detect a wrong split]
findings.impact: What remains unproven is only the live round-trip against Zarinpal's own sandbox: that a real merchant id is accepted, that their verify endpoint agrees with our stored amount, and that their redirect carries our signed state back intact. The capture logic itself - the 85/15 split, the escrow hold, the balanced payment_capture ledger event, replay idempotency and the refusal to capture on a rejected verification - is now executed by test/capture.test.js against a real PostgreSQL. This finding previously asserted the whole path had no executed evidence; that is no longer true and the claim is narrowed accordingly.
findings.remediation: Run audit/harness/e2e.mjs with AUDIT_ZARINPAL_MERCHANT_ID set to a real sandbox merchant id, then record the result with AUDIT_J5=VERIFIED AUDIT_J5_NOTE="..." python3 audit/mc_sim.py. The offline seam suggested here has been built; only the live provider call is outstanding.
